_origin: Start-Up campaign Phase 1 — 39 templates seeded with equipment_type null; the mint-candidate table was ruled in one pass.
_note: BASE-ONLY. Drafter field-def tables ride the next batch; Phase 2's standards research covers the new types. Minting a key is not the same as populating its nameplate.

mint.name: Water Tank
mint.why: 85 items across 5 masters. Distinct from expansion_tank, which is a pressurisation vessel on a closed loop, not a storage tank.

mint.name: Glycol Mixing & Fill Tank
mint.why: 47 items across 3 masters. It mixes and fills; expansion_tank absorbs. Different equipment, different start-up.

mint.name: Water Meter
mint.why: 45 items across 5 masters. No collision in the register.

mint.name: Plumbing Fixture
mint.why: 30 items across 6 masters. QUALIFIED DELIBERATELY: a bare `fixture` key would collide with lighting fixtures, and a key that reads two ways is a Law 8 hazard.

mint.name: Split System Air Conditioner
mint.why: 19 items. rtu and heat_pump are packaged units; a split system is two pieces with a line set between them, and its start-up differs at exactly that seam.

map.why: Dry vs evaporative is variant-as-data, not a type. Same RTU-vs-AHU bar.
A water-cooled DX unit is a chiller variant.
Already minted in the IST catalog addendum; the system decomposes into the two ruled keys.

leave.subject: Standpipe Systems
leave.why: MINT REFUSED BY RULING, and the reasoning is the durable part: sprinkler and standpipe are already kind='system' rows in the catalog. Minting an equipment key would put the same thing in two places. A start-up template wanting a home is a template-ATTACHMENT question, not a taxonomy one — a recorded ruling is not reversed to solve a keying problem.

leave.subject: Gas-Fluid Distribution
leave.why: A distribution system, not a unit.
